<aside class="blog-tldr not-prose"><div class="blog-tldr__label">TL;DR</div><div class="blog-tldr__body">
- Hospitals own full episode risk
- Five surgical categories count
- Thirty days post-discharge matter
- Leadership must redesign care paths
</div></aside>

Let me put this plainly. If your hospital is one of the 721 in the **CMS TEAM** model, Medicare is no longer just paying you for the operation — it’s holding you accountable for what happens for 30 days afterward, across five common surgeries. This started January 1, 2026.

## What does CMS TEAM mean for your hospital?

You keep billing fee-for-service, but CMS reconciles your actual spending against a target price. Beat it with good quality and you earn a bonus. Miss it, and starting in 2027 you write CMS a check.

## What's at stake financially?

Rainfall Health estimates up to 20% of Medicare revenue is at stake and up to $85 million in five-year upside for a system that gets this right — our own figures, not independently audited. Independent analysts are more cautious: Optum Advisory projects that "56% of mandatory participants are projected to lose money under current criteria unless they meaningfully improve performance," averaging $1.2 million per facility, and Brandeis University with the Institute for Accountable Care anticipates up to two-thirds of hospitals losing revenue on net. Either way, doing nothing is the expensive option.

## What should CEOs do — three moves

1. **Get your data house in order** across the full 30-day episode.
2. **Lock in post-acute partners** who deliver low readmissions (each one avoided saves roughly $14,000, per Milliman).
3. **Assign an owner and pick your track deliberately** before 2027 downside risk arrives.

<aside class="blog-callout blog-callout--default not-prose"><div class="blog-callout__body">

Rainfall Health is the first and only recognized standard for Medicare-mandated models like CMS TEAM — and we go at-risk alongside our hospital partners.

</div></aside>

## Frequently asked questions

### Did our hospital choose to be in CMS TEAM?

No — participation is mandatory for any IPPS hospital whose CMS Certification Number sits within one of the 188 selected Core-Based Statistical Areas (CBSAs).

### When do hospitals owe money under CMS TEAM?

Downside financial risk starts in Performance Year 2, calendar year 2027.

### How much upside does Rainfall Health estimate for CMS TEAM?

Rainfall Health estimates up to $85 million in five-year upside for a system that performs well — a company-stated figure, not independently audited.

### What should a hospital CEO do first for CMS TEAM?

Fix your episode data across the full 30-day window — this is the foundation every other TEAM initiative depends on.

### Who should own CMS TEAM inside a hospital?

A named executive should own it — most commonly someone in case management or population health.
